title: External validity — do the findings hold across multiple synthetic maps?
description: Studies 1-5 all reuse a single channel geometry, a single-graph external-validity bottleneck. This study replicates the baseline-fairness arms (DRL_no_chart / DRL_with_chart / RuleBased) across THREE distinct synthetic port maps (mapgen.js: map 0 = canonical anchor identical to all prior studies; map 2 = compact strongly-curved channels; map 3 = asymmetric long-north/short-south with an S-curve), under clean and harsh degradation, to test whether the chart-prior effect and the arm ordering generalize beyond the original graph. Only the geometry/topology changes across maps; kinematics, degradation, obstacles, metrics and the chart prior are identical.
research_question: Do (a) the chart prior closing the DRL-vs-rule-based gap and (b) the arm ordering hold across multiple distinct port geometries, not just the canonical map?
seed_policy: SAME 6 seeds per cell (paired). env_seed = 42 + seed. Map graph attributes seeded by (env_seed, mapId).

training.note: DRL arms train 130 episodes; RuleBased no training.

cells_breakdown: 3 maps x 3 arms x 2 conditions x 6 seeds = 108 cells, 30 eval eps each = 3,240 eval episodes

analysis_plan.omnibus: three-way factorial arm(3) x condition(2) x map(3) (+ seed), partial eta^2; the MAP main effect and arm x map interaction quantify cross-map generalization
analysis_plan.key_question: is the arm effect (esp. DRL_no_chart < DRL_with_chart) preserved across maps (small arm x map interaction), and does the map factor add variance without overturning the ordering?

scope_notes: Three synthetic geometries broaden but do not fully establish real-world external validity; still a synthesized testbed.
2 conditions (clean/harsh) x 6 seeds keeps the 3-map design computationally feasible.
Deployed web application unaffected; offline research.
